channel.title: The daily tape · compute.world
channel.description: The US remote-access rule moved from customs to credit this week. Nvidia told server partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on 26 November, and Bloomberg reported that lenders have paused or dropped loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent tenants, from Bridge Data Centres' $6.6 billion facility to a $372 million Digital Halo loan and a $480 million Aolani loan. Fitch said Asia-Pacific data centre investment will slow and that neoclouds face the most pressure; Reuters reported Z.AI's next flagship has slipped and Moonshot expects release cycles to double without offshore compute. In the US, S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance, while five-year default swaps for Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hit records. US markets are closed for Thanksgiving and other news was thin. List prices held for a fourteenth straight tape day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69 and Crusoe's 1 December step-up still pending.

item.title: Compute brief - 26 November 2026
item.description: The US remote-access rule moved from customs to credit this week. Nvidia told server partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on 26 November, and Bloomberg reported that lenders have paused or dropped loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent tenants, from Bridge Data Centres' $6.6 billion facility to a $372 million Digital Halo loan and a $480 million Aolani loan. Fitch said Asia-Pacific data centre investment will slow and that neoclouds face the most pressure; Reuters reported Z.AI's next flagship has slipped and Moonshot expects release cycles to double without offshore compute. In the US, S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance, while five-year default swaps for Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave hit records. US markets are closed for Thanksgiving and other news was thin. List prices held for a fourteenth straight tape day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69 and Crusoe's 1 December step-up still pending. Countries: Malaysia: Lenders pause Bridge Data Centres $6.6 billion loan diligence, one bank passes on $372 million Digital Halo loan; Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia (Wire, 26 Nov, single-source). Singapore: Banks reassess $480 million Aolani neocloud loan; Nvidia booked $104 billion of 2025 revenue through its Singapore unit; shipments halted (Wire, 26 Nov, single-source). China: Z.AI GLM-5.5 slips, Moonshot sees release cycles doubling without offshore compute (Reuters, 26 Nov, single-source); GDS cuts 2026 capex guide to about $1.2 billion from $1.5 billion (25 Nov). United States: S&P puts Nvidia AA on CreditWatch Negative; Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave CDS at records; Air Force seeks 30,000-GPU, about $2 billion supercomputer; Ohio approves 800 MW gas plant for EdgeConneX (Wire, 25 Nov). South Korea: KT Cloud takes all 60 MW of Keppel's Ansan AI data centre, ready 2030 (Wire, 26 Nov). Australia: Sharon AI installs 8,208 B300s in Sydney for ESDS; handover mid-December, billing January 2027 (Wire, 26 Nov). Portugal: Fortitude Capital plans 202 MW Hermes AI campus in Sines (Wire, 26 Nov, single-source).
